title: Course map

Start with [0.2 Your first notebook](00-start/02-first-notebook.ipynb). This first review edition contains two complete lessons. Every other lesson below is **coming soon**; the full course is not yet available. Lessons are designed for 20–40 minutes each.

Our running question is **Do people live longer in richer countries?** We return to the same country panel as your skills grow. Short examples use explicitly made-up numbers for fictional countries. A later person-level thread will use clearly labelled simulated data.

- 0.1 What Python is for in social science — coming soon
- **[0.2 Your first notebook, in the browser](00-start/02-first-notebook.ipynb) — available**

## Part 1 · Python basics — coming soon

1.1 Values and variables · 1.2 Lists and dictionaries · 1.3 Decisions and repetition · 1.4 Functions · 1.5 Reading error messages · 1.6 Importing libraries

Store country measurements, describe a survey respondent and write a growth-rate function. No computer-science background is assumed.

## Part 3 · Visualization — coming soon

3.1 First plots from a DataFrame · 3.2 Labels, scales and colour · 3.3 Comparing groups and small multiples · 3.4 Saving figures for papers and slides

Build the income–life expectancy scatter in small steps, then compare patterns across decades. A small multiple repeats the same chart for different groups.

## Part 4 · Statistics and regression — coming soon

4.1 Descriptive statistics and a Table 1 · 4.2 Correlation and simple OLS · 4.3 Multiple regression, categories and interactions · 4.4 Robust and clustered standard errors · 4.5 Fixed effects and panel models · 4.6 Regression tables

Learn what a model estimates and what it cannot establish. Ordinary least squares (OLS) fits a linear relationship; fixed effects account for group differences that stay constant over time. Instrumental variables and difference-in-differences are beyond the core path.

## Part 5 · A workflow others can rerun — coming soon

5.1 Optional local installation · 5.2 Folders, paths, notebooks and scripts · 5.3 Public data by code · 5.4 Checking AI coding assistance

Turn the running example into a project another person can rerun from raw data to results. Local installation stays optional.
